question: Which Indian ruler is famously known as the “Napoleon of India”?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Samudragupta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Samudragupta**, the second ruler of the Gupta Empire, is referred to as the **"Napoleon of India"** due to his extensive military conquests and strategic prowess.
 
• This title was given by the historian **Vincent A. Smith**, who admired Samudragupta's military achievements and compared him to Napoleon Bonaparte.
 
• Samudragupta ruled from approximately **335 CE to 380 CE** and expanded the Gupta Empire significantly through his campaigns in both northern and southern India.
 
• His conquests are detailed in the **Prayaga Prashasti** (Allahabad Pillar Inscription), composed by his court poet **Harisena**, which describes his victories over numerous kings and territories.
